bio_en: Mihran Sharoyan was born in Semal in Sasun in the 1900s, the son of Manuk Sharoyan, an educated revolutionary who had become a kind of prince of Sasun and its representative to the government. A serious, thoughtful pupil at the central school of Mush, he survived the Genocide; his uncle Stepan was killed at the capture of Vagharshapat in 1920. Under Soviet rule he was jailed for a year and a half over the killing of Khushoyan and acquitted under public pressure, then fled to the heights of Aragats when threatened with re-arrest. He and a companion, Hovhannes, were killed by Chekists in December, as reported in Droshak in June 1932.
notes: Compiled from the archive review, 2026-10-12. Confidence: medium. Death year not explicit (probably Dec 1931).
